title: Japanese Alphabet Flashcards
summary: Always-available hiragana, katakana, sound-change, and beginner word recall for short review sessions.
audience: English-speaking beginners learning to recognize and read Japanese kana.

cards.title: Hiragana Vowels
cards.prompt: Read あ・い・う・え・お before revealing the romaji.
cards.explanation: The readings are a, i, u, e, o. This vowel order organizes every kana row in the gojūon chart.

cards.title: Hiragana K Row
cards.prompt: Read か・き・く・け・こ aloud from left to right.
cards.explanation: The readings are ka, ki, ku, ke, ko. Keep the fixed vowel order a, i, u, e, o.

cards.title: Hiragana S Row
cards.prompt: Read さ・し・す・せ・そ and notice the irregular label.
cards.explanation: The readings are sa, shi, su, se, so. Learner romaji uses shi instead of a mechanical si.

cards.title: Hiragana T Row
cards.prompt: Read た・ち・つ・て・と and find the two irregular labels.
cards.explanation: The readings are ta, chi, tsu, te, to. Chi and tsu show the pronunciation more clearly than ti and tu.

cards.title: Hiragana N Row
cards.prompt: Read な・に・ぬ・ね・の without looking at a chart.
cards.explanation: The readings are na, ni, nu, ne, no. Compare ぬ and ね by following the loop and final tail.

cards.title: Hiragana H Row
cards.prompt: Read は・ひ・ふ・へ・ほ and recall the special middle sound.
cards.explanation: The readings are ha, hi, fu, he, ho. Japanese fu is lighter than a strongly lip-biting English f.

cards.title: Hiragana M Row
cards.prompt: Read ま・み・む・め・も from shape alone.
cards.explanation: The readings are ma, mi, mu, me, mo. Compare め with ぬ by tracking where the line exits the loop.

cards.title: Hiragana Y Row
cards.prompt: Which three basic sounds are written や・ゆ・よ?
cards.explanation: They are ya, yu, yo. Modern basic Japanese has no separate yi or ye kana in this row.

cards.title: Hiragana R Row
cards.prompt: Read ら・り・る・れ・ろ with one light Japanese r sound.
cards.explanation: The readings are ra, ri, ru, re, ro. The consonant is a brief tongue tap rather than a strong English r.

cards.title: Hiragana Final Row
cards.prompt: Read わ・を・ん and recall where each appears.
cards.explanation: They are wa, object-particle o, and moraic n. を is typed wo even though beginners normally pronounce it o.

cards.title: Compare Ki And Sa
cards.prompt: What visual detail separates き from さ?
cards.explanation: き has two horizontal crossings near the top, while さ has one. Compare the complete shapes, not only the curve.

cards.title: Compare Ru And Ro
cards.prompt: Which one closes with a small loop: る or ろ?
cards.explanation: る closes with a small loop at the bottom. ろ keeps the corresponding lower curve open.

cards.title: Dakuten Voices K
cards.prompt: Read the change か → が and name both sounds.
cards.explanation: か is ka. Adding dakuten voices the consonant, producing が ga and throat vibration.

cards.title: The Circle Makes P
cards.prompt: What does the small circle do in は → ぱ?
cards.explanation: Handakuten changes h-row kana to p sounds. は ha becomes ぱ pa; the same rule gives pi, pu, pe, po.

cards.title: Small Tsu Holds
cards.prompt: Contrast きて kite with きって kitte.
cards.explanation: Small っ creates a brief closure and doubles the following consonant in romaji and common IME input.

cards.title: Small Yo Contracts
cards.prompt: Contrast きよ ki-yo with きょ kyo.
cards.explanation: Full-size よ begins a new mora. Small ょ combines with the preceding i-row kana into one contracted sound.

cards.title: Long A Changes Meaning
cards.prompt: Which is grandmother: おばさん or おばあさん?
cards.explanation: おばあさん obaasan is grandmother. The extra あ lengthens the vowel; おばさん obasan means aunt.

cards.title: Katakana Vowels
cards.prompt: Read ア・イ・ウ・エ・オ using the sounds you already know.
cards.explanation: They are a, i, u, e, o. Katakana changes the shapes, not the underlying five-vowel system.

cards.title: Katakana K Row
cards.prompt: Read カ・キ・ク・ケ・コ from left to right.
cards.explanation: The readings are ka, ki, ku, ke, ko. Connect each sound to its hiragana partner only as a temporary bridge.

cards.title: Katakana S Row
cards.prompt: Read サ・シ・ス・セ・ソ and identify shi.
cards.explanation: The readings are sa, shi, su, se, so. シ is shi and belongs in the i position of the row.

cards.title: Katakana T Row
cards.prompt: Read タ・チ・ツ・テ・ト and identify chi and tsu.
cards.explanation: The readings are ta, chi, tsu, te, to. The sound pattern exactly matches the hiragana t-row.

cards.title: Katakana N Row
cards.prompt: Read ナ・ニ・ヌ・ネ・ノ without romaji.
cards.explanation: The readings are na, ni, nu, ne, no. ノ is a single falling stroke and appears inside many loanwords.

cards.title: Katakana H Row
cards.prompt: Read ハ・ヒ・フ・ヘ・ホ and identify fu.
cards.explanation: The readings are ha, hi, fu, he, ho. フ is a one-stroke fu, often confused with ワ or ウ at first.

cards.title: Katakana M Row
cards.prompt: Read マ・ミ・ム・メ・モ from shape alone.
cards.explanation: The readings are ma, mi, mu, me, mo. ミ has three descending horizontal strokes; ム begins with a triangle-like form.

cards.title: Katakana Y Row
cards.prompt: Read the three basic y-row symbols ヤ・ユ・ヨ.
cards.explanation: They are ya, yu, yo. ユ has two strokes and ヨ has three horizontal levels.

cards.title: Katakana R Row
cards.prompt: Read ラ・リ・ル・レ・ロ with a light tongue tap.
cards.explanation: The readings are ra, ri, ru, re, ro. ロ is the box-shaped ro; do not confuse it with the kanji 口 without context.

cards.title: Katakana Final Row
cards.prompt: Read ワ・ヲ・ン and recall the modern sound of ヲ.
cards.explanation: They are wa, usually o, and moraic n. Katakana ヲ is uncommon in ordinary beginner loanwords.

cards.title: Shi Or Tsu
cards.prompt: Compare シ and ツ: which one has more horizontal short strokes?
cards.explanation: シ shi has short strokes that sit more horizontally. ツ tsu has short strokes that stand more vertically.

cards.title: So Or N
cards.prompt: Compare ソ and ン: which long stroke rises from lower left?
cards.explanation: ン n rises from lower left. ソ so begins higher and falls down toward the left; stroke direction is the clue.

cards.title: Long Vowel Mark
cards.prompt: What sound job does ー perform in コーヒー?
cards.explanation: The mark extends the preceding vowel. コー is koo and ヒー is hii, giving koohii, coffee.

cards.title: Read A Loanword
cards.prompt: Read コーヒー one kana and sound extension at a time.
cards.explanation: コ ko + ー long o + ヒ hi + ー long i gives koohii, the Japanese loanword for coffee.

cards.title: Read Hotel
cards.prompt: Read ホテル before using the familiar English word as a clue.
cards.explanation: ホ ho + テ te + ル ru gives hoteru. Japanese loanwords follow Japanese mora timing rather than English spelling.

cards.title: Read Restaurant
cards.prompt: Break レストラン into kana-sized beats.
cards.explanation: レ re + ス su + ト to + ラ ra + ン n gives resutoran, restaurant.

cards.title: Written Ha, Spoken Wa
cards.prompt: Why is こんばんは read konbanwa but typed konbanha?
cards.explanation: The final は is the topic particle. Learner romaji shows its spoken wa; the IME keys create the written kana ha.
